text: It's my fifth job interview this month and I'm running out of savings. The phone hasn't rung. I keep checking it anyway. The eviction notice came yesterday and rent is due next week. I don't know who else to call. I started writing a list of people I haven't asked yet, then crossed out the names I'd already tried. The list is short.

I just learned my coworker has been taking credit for my work for two years. Everyone in the meeting was praising her for the project I built alone. I sat there smiling. My jaw is sore from clenching it. After the meeting I walked to my car the long way, around the building, until I could trust myself to drive.

There's someone trying the door handle. Slowly. Then again. I can hear breathing on the other side. My phone is in the kitchen. I'm in the bedroom. The lock isn't strong. I crouched behind the bed. I don't know if they can hear me. I don't know if they're alone. The handle moves again.

The biopsy results were supposed to come Tuesday. It's Friday now. The portal keeps showing pending. I've checked it nineteen times today. My doctor's office said they'd call. They haven't. I made tea and forgot about it. I made another tea. I keep starting tasks and abandoning them halfway.

I lied to my friend about why I missed her wedding. I told her my flight was cancelled. The truth is I didn't want to face her father after what happened in May. She found out last week. She still hasn't replied to my text. I keep rereading what I sent, looking for what I should have written instead.

I made dinner for two by accident. I always do, even after a year. I ate standing up at the counter and watched a show I'd already seen, then started another one to make the apartment feel less quiet. The neighbors were having people over. I could hear them laughing through the wall.

The acceptance letter came in the regular mail like it was nothing. I read it three times standing in my driveway. Then I called my mom and we both started laughing and couldn't stop. I bought a cake from the bakery I couldn't normally afford. I keep grinning at strangers. They grin back.

I let the coffee go cold while watching my dog sleep in the patch of sun on the carpet. I had a list of things to do today. I'm going to do exactly none of them. The light is good. The radio is playing something I don't recognize. I don't feel like changing it.

Three more rejection letters this week. Twenty-seven this year. The only feedback was that they received many qualified applicants. I logged into the bank app, looked at the number, closed it. Tomorrow I'll do something. Maybe. The application portal is still open in another tab. I haven't touched it.

I still set out two coffee cups in the morning. I caught myself last week and stood at the counter for a long time before I put one back. Her sweater is still on the hook by the door. I don't know what to do with it. I haven't moved any of her things. The kitchen smells the same as it did.
